name: Winn Memorial Library
key_features: Romanesque Revival library built 1876–79 and now a National Historic Landmark.

name: Wembley Stadium
key_features: A tilted steel arch carries much of the roof, letting movable roof panels open over the pitch.

name: David S. Ingalls Rink
key_features: Yale's hockey rink, nicknamed "The Whale", with a ceiling up to 75 feet high.

name: Documentation Center Nazi Party Rally Grounds
key_features: A glass-and-steel shaft stabs diagonally through the unfinished Nazi Congress Hall.

name: Palm Springs Art Museum
key_features: 75,000 sq ft Modernist building; listed on the National Register in 2016.

name: Sultan Abdul Samad Building
by: A. C. Norman, R. A. J. Bidwell and A. B. Hubback
key_features: 41 m clock tower in the Indo-Saracenic manner, with copper-clad onion domes on three towers.

name: Teatro degli Arcimboldi
key_features: Fan-shaped, 2,375-seat theatre inside a converted Pirelli factory in Bicocca.

name: Egyptian Museum
key_features: Neoclassical facade; halls arranged in chronological sequence, statues on the ground floor, funerary items above.

name: Government House, Yerevan
key_features: Tamanian's north-west wing built 1926-29; his son Gevorg finished the rest by 1941.

name: Copenhagen Opera House
key_features: Large cantilevered roof over a glazed foyer facing the harbour.

name: General Rafael Urdaneta Bridge
key_features: Prestressed concrete bridge over Lake Maracaibo, completed 1962.

name: Custom House, Shanghai
key_features: Four Doric columns mark the main entrance; the eastern section is eight storeys facing the Huangpu River.

name: Republican Palace, Baghdad
key_features: Modernist palace first designed as a central domed section with two wings; fountain in front part of original design.

name: United States Institute of Peace Headquarters
key_features: Environmentally friendly building near the National Mall, noted for its unique roof.

name: Basilica of the Holy Trinity
key_features: Low circular church seating about 9,000 under one column-free roof.

name: Tokyo Big Sight
key_features: Four inverted pyramids raised on legs above a plaza hold the conference halls.

name: Palau Güell
key_features: Parabolic-arched gates and a central hall under a perforated dome, topped by mosaic chimneys.

name: Quinta Monroy
key_features: 'Half a good house': the state builds half and families build the rest.

name: Pakistan National Art Gallery
by: Suhail Abbasi and Naeem Pasha (Suhail & Pasha)
key_features: Four-storey brick cube with 14 galleries, lecture halls and a 400-seat auditorium; won a 1989 design contest.

name: Puente de Occidente
key_features: Suspension bridge over the Cauca River, 291 m long, opened 1895.

name: Hecht Synagogue
key_features: Built of Jerusalem stone with a women's section on the gallery floor, on the Mount Scopus campus.

name: Milano Centrale
key_features: 200 m facade and a 72 m high vault, with steel canopies 341 m long over 24 platforms; Liberty and Art Deco blend.

name: Chapelle du Rosaire
key_features: White tile walls and stained glass in blue, green and yellow fill the chapel with coloured light.

name: Clyfford Still Museum
key_features: Single-artist museum with nine galleries and two outdoor terraces.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
key_features: Circular open plan under a tent-like copper roof so the whole crowd can see the image.

name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art
key_features: Galleries spiral down around a central ramp, lit by roof lanterns derived from windcatchers.

name: Toblerone Tower (Karaburma)
key_features: Hexagonal-plan residential tower in prestressed concrete, built 1960–63; it won a design award.

name: Vietnam National Convention Center
key_features: Long hall under a wave-shaped roof that rolls along the facade, echoing the sea.

name: Za-Koenji Public Theatre
key_features: Tent-like dark steel-plate concrete shell, its roof carved by cones and cylinders, pricked with small glazed portholes.

name: Shoji Ueda Museum of Photography
key_features: Museum devoted solely to the photographer Shoji Ueda, founded in 1995 with over 12,000 works.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus)
by: Frederick William Stevens (from an initial design by Axel Haig)
key_features: Indo-Saracenic and Victorian Gothic Revival railway terminus with 18 platforms; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.

name: Paul VI Audience Hall
key_features: Undulating vault of prefabricated concrete elements on inclined supports spans the hall.

name: Royal Albert Hall
by: Francis Fowke and Henry Y. D. Scott
key_features: Elliptical red-brick drum with a terracotta frieze, under a wrought-iron and glass dome.

name: BOK Center
by: César Pelli (Pelli Clarke Pelli), MATRIX Architects, Odell Associates
key_features: Glass facade of 1,600 panels leaning five degrees, wrapped by about 33,000 stainless-steel panels in an upward spiral.

name: Church of Our Lady Queen of Poland (Lord's Ark)
key_features: Sloping roof and 70 m crowned-cross mast recall Noah's Ark; first new church in Nowa Huta, 1967–77.

name: Vyborg Library
key_features: Built 1927–1935 and restored in a project completed in 2013.

name: African Renaissance Monument
key_features: 50 m bronze figure group of a family on a hill in Ouakam, overlooking the Atlantic.

name: Edmund Barton Building
key_features: Large office building on the National Triangle in Barton, designed by Harry Seidler.

name: Nebotičnik
key_features: Tower with sculpted façade and a café on the eleventh storey; construction began April 1931, opened 21 February 1933.

name: New Town Hall, Hanover
key_features: An eclectic palace-like town hall with a central dome climbed by a curved, inclined lift.

name: Osaka International Convention Center (Grand Cube Osaka)
key_features: Convention centre in Osaka with its own underground station on the Keihan Nakanoshima line.

name: Library and Learning Center, Vienna University of Economics
key_features: Walls leaning at 35 degrees and a massive black volume cantilevered at an angle over the campus plaza.

name: Altes Museum
key_features: Neoclassical museum fronted by a colonnade of eighteen Ionic columns facing the Lustgarten.

name: Barbican Estate
key_features: A walkway city of housing, arts centre, lake and conservatory above the street.

name: Biblioteca cantonale, Lugano
key_features: Ticino's key modernist work, in Parco Ciani: an L-plan library with a windowless, Bauhaus-inspired book-stack wing.

name: Boston City Hall
key_features: An inverted ziggurat whose form shows the city government's functions from outside.

name: BP Pedestrian Bridge
key_features: Serpentine 935 ft girder bridge clad in stainless steel; links Millennium Park and Maggie Daley Park.

name: Brussels-Central Station
key_features: Station halls set into the slope above the underground North-South rail link.

name: Cairo International Stadium
key_features: Olympic-standard multi-use stadium with an all-seated capacity of 75,000.

name: Sevilla Tower
key_features: César Pelli's 180-metre Seville office tower, the tallest building in Andalusia, completed in 2015.

name: Open Chapel of Lomas de Cuernavaca (Palmira Chapel)
by: Félix Candela, with Guillermo Rosell and Manuel Larrosa
key_features: A single 4 cm hyperbolic-paraboloid saddle that opens 30 m wide at the front and rises to a 21 m point.

name: Capital Gate
key_features: A diagrid tower leaning 18 degrees, held back by a pre-cambered concrete core.

name: Carré d'Art
key_features: Glass arts centre facing the Roman Maison Carrée, with a thin canopy on five slender columns; half is underground.

name: Cartagena Roman Theatre Museum
key_features: A route through a palace, a tunnel and a ruined church climbs to the restored Roman theatre.

name: CCTV Headquarters
key_features: A loop of two leaning towers joined by a 75-metre cantilever.

name: Galician Centre of Contemporary Art (CGAC)
key_features: Granite-clad wedges beside a convent, with a deep cut-away entrance porch and a roof terrace over the old town.

name: Chiesa Madre di Gibellina
key_features: A great white sphere set on a cubic block, built in the new town after the 1968 Belice earthquake.

name: Church of San Giovanni Battista
key_features: Elliptical stone church with a sloping glass roof, walls banded in white marble and grey granite.

name: Cinémathèque française (former American Center)
key_features: Stone-clad block whose park side breaks into tilting, folding forms under a curling zinc roof.

name: Avery Coonley House
key_features: Prairie-style house of 1908–09 with the ground floor treated as a basement; landscape by Jens Jensen.

name: David and Gladys Wright House
key_features: A curved Wright house on seven piers, wrapped around a courtyard and reached by a spiral ramp.

name: Heichal HaTarbut (Charles Bronfman Auditorium)
by: Dov Karmi, Ze'ev Rechter and Yaakov Rechter
key_features: Largest concert hall in Tel Aviv; opened October 1957 at Habima Square.

name: Museum Liner (Kunstmuseum Appenzell)
key_features: Galleries under a saw-tooth of gables of varying height, roof and walls clad in overlapping stainless-steel sheets.

name: Palacio Municipal de Montevideo (Intendencia)
key_features: City hall on 18 de Julio Avenue, cut from a planned 114 m to 78 m.

name: Palau de la Música Catalana
key_features: Steel frame allows walls of glass and a stained-glass skylight over the concert hall.

name: SDU Campus Kolding
key_features: Triangular university building wrapped in perforated steel shutters that open and close with the daylight.

name: 20 Fenchurch Street
key_features: Top-heavy form that bursts upward and outward, with a sky garden at the top.

name: AaltoAlvari swimming hall
key_features: Alvar Aalto's swimming hall on Seminaarinmäki in Jyväskylä, before its later extension.

name: Abdeen Palace
key_features: Palace built 1863-1874, adorned with paintings and many gold-decorated clocks.

name: Alamillo Bridge
key_features: A single leaning pylon, 142 m tall, balances the deck with its own weight, with no back-stay cables.

name: Alden B. Dow Home and Studio
key_features: Home and studio of the architect, who was associated with Frank Lloyd Wright.

name: Aluminaire House
by: A. Lawrence Kocher and Albert Frey
key_features: Roughly cubic, about 1,200 sq ft, on six columns; corrugated metal over steel angles.

name: Amsterdam Orphanage (Burgerweeshuis)
key_features: Repeated domed units clustered along diagonal internal streets make the orphanage a small city.

name: Angkor Wat
key_features: Concentric galleries and a wide moat lead along a west-facing axis to a quincunx of towers.

name: Appleby Blue Almshouse
key_features: Almshouse flats for older people in brick ranges round a planted courtyard, reached by shared timber-lined galleries.

name: Archaeological Museum of Ioannina
key_features: Concrete frame filled with local stone, low pavilions round a courtyard in a park.

name: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
key_features: Galleries ringed around a tall circular atrium climbed by a spiralling ramp.

name: Bensberg Town Hall
key_features: Concrete town hall built into a medieval castle's ruins, crowned by a jagged stair tower.

name: Bishop Edward King Chapel
key_features: Elliptical chapel walled in patterned stone; inside, a grove of timber columns under a high clerestory.

name: Bodegas Ysios
key_features: An undulating aluminium roof over cedar-clad walls echoes the mountain ridge behind the winery.

name: Caltrans District 7 Headquarters
key_features: Office slab wrapped in a perforated aluminium skin whose panels open and close with the sun.

name: Canary Wharf Underground Station
key_features: Glass canopies pour daylight into a vast concrete hall dug into a former dock.

name: Canton Tower
key_features: Hyperboloid lattice of inclined steel columns twisted by two rotated ellipses to a narrow waist.

name: Casa no Butantã (Paulo Mendes da Rocha House)
key_features: One raised concrete floor on just four pillars; closed end walls, long window bands to east and west.

name: Casa da Música
key_features: A faceted concrete solid with the concert hall cut straight through it, glazed at both ends.

name: Casa Ugalde
key_features: White walls fanned out across a hillside toward the sea, shaped around the views and existing trees.

name: Cathedral Church of Christ
key_features: Norman Gothic cathedral begun in 1924; oldest Anglican cathedral in the Church of Nigeria.

name: Cayan Tower
key_features: Each floor rotates slightly on the one below so the tower twists a quarter turn from base to top.

name: Centre Point
key_features: A 34-storey tower of precast fine-concrete segments using crushed Portland stone.

name: Chowdiah Memorial Hall
key_features: 1,100-seat auditorium built in the shape of a gigantic seven-stringed violin; completed 1980.

name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
key_features: Wraps the steel trusses of an unfinished abattoir hall; three 32 m glass Serres have no frames or fins.

name: City Hall and Central Library, The Hague
key_features: Two white slabs enclose a vast glass-roofed atrium crossed by bridges, nicknamed the Ice Palace.

name: Coltejer Building
by: Raúl Fajardo, Aníbal Saldarriaga, Germán Samper, Jorge Manjarres
key_features: Medellín tower built for the Coltejer textile company, completed 1972.

name: Communal House of the Textile Institute
key_features: A Constructivist landmark in Moscow, a 1929–31 student dormitory designed by Ivan Nikolaev for 2,000 students.

name: Crypt of Colonia Guell
key_features: Leaning columns and vaults found with a hanging chain model of catenary forces.

name: Dallas City Hall
key_features: Concrete wedge whose front leans out over the plaza, each floor projecting beyond the one below.

name: De Kunstlinie
key_features: One flat glass-edged box packs theatre halls, studios and small courtyards side by side by the lake.

name: Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo House-Studio
key_features: Two functionalist studio houses, red and blue, joined by a roof bridge, with sawtooth roof lights.

name: Everett McKinley Dirksen United States Courthouse
key_features: Mies's steel-and-glass courthouse tower of 1964, 384 ft tall, on the Federal Center plaza.

name: Domain Park Flats
key_features: 20-storey slab facing the Botanic Gardens; windows and balconies are laid out freely to show each flat's size.
